t: The Score of Students Solving Math Expression: Interval DP over Achievable Values
o:
**Understanding the problem**

Students may apply the operators in any order (any full parenthesization) with correct arithmetic; a submission equal to the true value earns 5 points, a value some other grouping produces earns 2, anything else 0. For "7+3*1*2": proper precedence gives 7+(3*1*2) = 13, so answering 13 earns 5; the left-to-right grouping yields ((7+3)*1)*2 = 20, worth 2; and 42 is unreachable, scoring 0 — total 7. Example 2 repeats the pattern for "3+5*2": three students answering the true 13 get 5 each and two answering (3+5)*2 = 16 get 2 each, totaling 19. Example 3 highlights the tie-break: in "6+0*1" both orders evaluate to 6, but a correct answer always earns 5, never 2. With at most 15 operators there can be roughly ten million raw groupings (a Catalan number), so caching sub-results separates feasible from hopeless.
k: Every 'wrong order' value is exactly a value produced by fully parenthesizing the expression, so the task reduces to collecting all results over all binary parenthesis trees.
Subexpression outcomes depend only on the substring, giving interval DP: memo[l][r] is the set of values achievable from s[l..r], merged over each operator split.
The correct answer takes precedence (5 points) even when another order also produces it; grade each submission with O(1) set lookups while keeping multiplicities.
Intermediate products can exceed the final bound, so carry 64-bit integers in typed languages.

a.i: Any way of inserting parentheses corresponds to splitting the expression at some operator, solving both sides independently, and combining every left value with every right value. Recursing over all splits enumerates exactly the student-interpretable values. Without memoization identical substrings are re-solved exponentially often, which collapses beyond a dozen operators, but it defines precisely the states the optimal method will cache.
s: values(i, j): if the substring is a single digit, return just that number.
Otherwise, for every operator position p inside the substring, gather values(i, p-1) and values(p+1, j).
Insert every sum and product of paired results into one set.
Compute the correct answer separately with standard precedence: multiply within each plus-separated term, then add the terms.
Score each submission: 5 if equal to the correct value, else 2 if found in the set, else 0.
a.t: Exponential — roughly Catalan(operators) combine operations because overlapping subproblems are recomputed; unusable near the 15-operator limit.
a.sp: O(operators) recursion depth plus transient per-split result sets.

a.n: Approach 2: Bottom-Up Interval DP over Value Sets
a.i: Cache the achievable-value set per substring so every interval is solved once. Digits occupy even indices and operators odd ones, so intervals of interest have odd length. Filling by increasing length merges dp[i][p-1] with dp[p+1][j] at each operator split; sets stay small because operands are single digits and products are bounded, and hashing makes grading each of up to 10^4 submissions an O(1) lookup. This is the boolean-parenthesization skeleton generalized to arbitrary integer results.
s: Initialize dp[i][i] as the singleton digit set for every digit cell.
For interval lengths 3, 5, ... up to n, allocate an empty set for each interval [i, j].
For every odd split p inside (i, j), merge dp[i][p-1] and dp[p+1][j], inserting sums or products according to the operator at p.
Compute the true answer with a running product per plus-separated term.
Sum 5 / 2 / 0 points per submission using set membership in dp[0][n-1].
a.t: O(n^3 * S^2) worst case with S the largest value-set size — three nested interval loops times pairwise merging; sets stay tiny in practice.
a.sp: O(n^2 * S) — one hash set of reachable values per interval.

w:
**Takeaway**

Bring up Approach 2: interval DP over value sets is the canonical tool for "enumerate every way to parenthesize". Pitfalls: awarding 2 points when a wrong-order grouping coincides with the correct value — the 5-point rule wins (Example 3); forgetting that duplicate submissions each score; and overflowing 32-bit accumulators on adversarial inputs. Natural follow-ups: count the distinct achievable values, or reconstruct a parenthesization reaching a given wrong answer.
